title: THE RED DAWN
subtitle: A Speculative Installation About Belief and Manufactured Reality
summary: A future religion built from the visual and psychological machinery of online conspiracy.
statement: When does information become belief, and when does belief become reality?
body: Set on the eve of 2090, The Red Dawn imagines the Nibiru conspiracy evolving into a digital cult. Screens, fibre optics, printed social feeds, propaganda film and ritual posture form an installation that asks visitors to enter a belief system rather than observe it from outside.

partners.name: Royal College of Art · MA Information Experience Design

sections.title: The Installation
sections.body: The final work stages Nibiru as the centre of a future religion. A suspended red planet, mirrored surfaces, illuminated cables, phones and printed feeds turn online conspiracy into a physical place of worship.
sections.caption: 01 / FINAL WORK

blocks.title: The shrine and its worshipper
blocks.body: The visitor sits or kneels before a red screen while the structure rises above the body. Looking becomes submission; an online fiction acquires the scale and posture of an institution.
blocks.caption: FINAL INSTALLATION / RCA DEGREE SHOW

blocks.title: Recruitment Film
blocks.body: A portrait recruitment film designed to circulate from inside the imagined organisation. It introduces the prophecy before the installation reveals the machinery that sustains it.
blocks.caption: PROPAGANDA FILM

prophecies.title: THE ONE GOD
prophecies.body: Nibiru shall replace the sun and rise from the horizon, burning away all sins.

prophecies.title: THE ONE END
prophecies.body: Anunnaki shall shatter the human regime. In the Red Dawn, a new order shall arise.

blocks.title: The network made physical
blocks.body: Phones orbit the central body as witnesses. Their posts continue downward as printed evidence, while exposed cables and the prophecy screen make the infrastructure of belief visible.
blocks.caption: PHONE ORBIT / PRINTED FEED / PROPHECY SCREEN

blocks.title: A simulated Nibiru community
blocks.body: Ambiguous photographs of suns, moons and planets accumulate inside a closed social community. Repetition turns each uncertain image into support for the next one; the digital feed is later printed into the installation.
blocks.caption: DIGITAL COMMUNITY / IMAGE ECHO CHAMBER

sections.title: The Ritual
sections.body: One gesture completes the work: the visitor kneels. Screens, sound and red light prepare the scene, but the meaning changes only when the body accepts the posture of worship.
sections.caption: 02 / EXPERIENCE

blocks.title: From shrine sketch to encounter
blocks.body: The early study defines the mirrored planet, six screens, projected narrative, fibre optics and the place where the visitor would kneel. The final work keeps this bodily relationship at its centre.

blocks.title: Audience Testing
blocks.body: Visitors discussed the work while standing inside its light, sound and image field. Their responses tested whether the encounter communicated worship, community and the uneasy attraction of a closed information system.
blocks.caption: AUDIENCE TEST / INSTALLATION FEEDBACK

sections.title: Constructing Belief
sections.body: The system emerged through interviews, perception testing and field observation. Each step moves from lived vulnerability to the social machinery that can transform uncertain images into collective belief.
sections.caption: 03 / RESEARCH TO SYSTEM

blocks.note: In times of uncertainty or personal crisis, conspiracy theories can offer control and belonging. They address dissatisfaction while strengthening personal and group identity.

blocks.alt: Perception workshop materials and coded results showing a 65 percent error rate
blocks.title: Perception workshop
blocks.body: Participants classified ambiguous photographs as the sun, moon or another planet. Sixty-five percent of the classifications were incorrect: context changed what people believed they could see.
blocks.caption: TEST MATERIAL / RESPONSE SHEETS / ERROR RATE 65%

sections.title: Artist Statement
sections.body: Whispering Behind is a two-channel experimental film that places the visible world beside an alternative reality forming inside the mind of a conspiracy believer. Murmured monologue, personal testimony and interview material allow both worlds to unfold in parallel.
sections.caption: 04 / PERSONAL TESTIMONY

blocks.title: Whispering Behind
blocks.body: Across two opposing channels, documentary reality and an imagined world diverge and contaminate one another, tracing how a conspiracy believer constructs an alternative reality through murmured monologue, self-narration and interview.
blocks.caption: TWO-CHANNEL EXPERIMENTAL FILM / MONOLOGUE / INTERVIEW
